items.title: Autonomous 5-ton John Deere skid-steer loader trained to perform acrobatic maneuvers using AI
items.summary: Videos of an incredibly acrobatic, nimble, and graceful John Deere 332G 5-tonne skid-steer loader have been shared by a group of researchers from the U.S. and Switzerland.
items.body: Videos of an incredibly acrobatic, nimble, and graceful John Deere 5-ton skid-steer loader have been shared by a group of researchers from the U.S. and Switzerland. A recently published paper titled Heavy Metal Acrobatics provides the reasoning behind this eyebrow-raising autonomous robotics feat. It is hoped this research will be useful in the future automation of heavy machinery in industries like construction, mining, and material handling. It also demonstrates that reinforcement learning in a simulation can transfer remarkably well to the real world. Researchers have used reinforcement learning to teach a 5-tonne John Deere skid-steer loader to perform complex acrobatic manoeuvres autonomously. Trained in simulation and transferred to a real machine, the system can balance on two wheels, navigate rough terrain, spin, and control its bucket before landing safely. items.title: New Windows 11 lock screen zero-day unlocks BitLocker-protected PCs with just a few keystrokes
items.summary: Windows 0-day lets attackers run software by partially bypass the lock screen with just some keystrokes — even BitLocker-protected machines are seemingly vulnerable
items.body: Considering the current status of the cybersecurity landscape, some may well say that "0-day" has lost its meaning, The latest high-stakes vulnerability pertains to a bug in Windows 11 (and possibly 10), wherein an attacker can partially bypass the lock screen and run software as the logged-in user, and seemingly access their data. If true, the vulnerability means even BitLocker won't help keep users' files protected. Unsurprisingly, the bug was discovered by Abdelhamid Naceri, the prolific Windows hacker known to the world as Nightmare Eclipse, and is responsible for about a dozen zero-day findings in Microsoft's operating system. The exploit requires physical access to the machine, but that's precisely the scenario that lock screens and/or BitLocker are supposed to protect against. To trigger the vulnerability, all you need is a keyboard. In the Windows 11 lock screen, click "Forgot my PIN," then hit Win+U to bring up the voice narrator. The window will be hidden behind the lock screen, which, for practical purposes, is just a veneer, but you can interact with it using the keyboard if you hold down the Caps Lock key and use the arrows and Enter. items.title: AI data center power demand will double by 2030 thanks to $4 trillion in spending, adding an entire Great Britain to energy strain
items.summary: IEA's report says that power production and distribution is barely keeping up with the rapid growth of AI data centers.
items.body: The AI data center build-out is pushing electricity grids across the globe, with many regions facing demand from projects that would exceed the current peak load that each system could support. According to the International Energy Agency’s (IEA) World Energy Outlook 2026 report , a total of 120GW of capacity is currently available across all types of data centers across the globe, with another 120GW expected to be completed by the end of the decade, 75% of which would be dedicated to artificial intelligence. Aside from that, it’s also tracking 93 large “AI factories” that are either under construction or being expanded via satellite imagery. It estimates that the capacity for these sites grew from under 2GW to 17GW in just two years, and that they’re expected to hit a total of 50GW upon completion, the equivalent of adding a second Great Britain to power demand. Reading the intro, you might have wondered if this work had a ReactOS connection, and indeed there is. items.body: Lip-Bu Tan, chief executive of Intel, said on Thursday that yields of chips made using the company's latest 18A (1.8nm-class) fabrication process have achieved 70%, which is more or less in line with what one would expect from an all-new manufacturing technology at this stage of its ramp. In addition, Intel and Microsoft have signed an agreement under which Microsoft will secure Intel Xeon supply capacity for years to come and will use Intel's EMIB advanced packaging technology for in-house silicon. "When I took over [as CEO in March, 2025], 18A yield was horrible; now we are at 70%," Lip-Bu Tan said at the TomorrowX conference (via @firesidealpha ). Lip-Bu Tan did not specify whether he meant functional yield, parametric yield, or percentage of sellable silicon. However, it is reasonable to expect a CEO of a semiconductor company to talk about functional die yield, the percentage of dies that pass basic electrical and functional testing. items.body: Pakistan's telecommunications authority, the PTA, has confirmed that internet connectivity issues affecting the country's residents are related to the failure of an international submarine cable. SEA-ME-WE 5 is located almost seven miles off the coast of Pakistan, near the Gulf of Oman and the Strait of Hormuz, and connects the region with European networks via the Middle East. The TWA says that the outage may have caused intermittent connectivity issues and a decline in service quality, with Transworld Associates (TWA) working to identify the cause of the issue. No timeframe has been provided for when a fix will be available yet, but for now, internet traffic has been rerouted to minimize the impact of the outage. The outage comes weeks after the Islamic Republic of Iran described several undersea fiber cables that run through the Strait of Hormuz as "legitimate new targets" in the ongoing tensions in the area. items.body: Intel’s next-gen Xeon Diamond Rapids CPUs appeared at Supercomputing 2026 ( SC26 ) in two separate booths, but neither was from Intel directly. Most interesting was a running server at the CXL booth, showcasing a demo with a Diamond Rapids CPU. The server ran for the first day of the show, and upon returning to the booth, we were informed that it had been shut down due to noise complaints (it’s hard to mistake a running server). Elsewhere at Bull’s booth, a Diamond Rapids CPU was shown installed in a server behind a glass case. Notably, Intel didn’t have a Diamond Rapids demo, instead focusing most of its booth on Xeon 6+ and its new D270 GPU, otherwise known as Crescent Island . The demo in question is for Montage’s CXL MXC, or Memory eXpander Controller. If you’re unfamiliar, memory expansion via CXL is an increasingly common tactic to give multi-host environments access to a large pool of memory, breaking free of an individual server’s capacity via CXL. items.body: A homelab builder benchmarked three used Nvidia V100s on Qwen 3.6 35B, achieving about 100 tokens per second in a custom setup costing $1,042 with just “e-waste” GPUs. The smaller, dense Qwen 3.6 27B manages about 24 tokens per second on the same platform, and the V100s use about half the energy of the same number of P100s for a given job. A ~$1k GPU box full of "e-waste" (V100, P100) cards competes with modern hardware/inference APIs. The test uses llama.cpp and covers more than 130 LLM tests, including Qwen 2.5, Gemma 4, and, of course, Qwen 3.6, at Q4/Q8/F16 precisions and from 4K to 128K context sizes. items.body: We've just had a few high-stakes security vulnerabilities making systems administrators run around with their heads on fire, and the deluge doesn't look like it's stopping any time soon. Java, the programming language that Oracle has always claimed is on billions of devices, has a critical security vulnerability that allows for remote code execution (RCE), often without even needing to log in to the application. The consequence is that an attacker can gain access to the target system, read user and internal data, and have a launch point for further shenanigans, including database access and potential system takeover. The flaw was dubbed Java4Shell by Calif Research, the lab that found the vulnerability. The researchers say it rates 9.2 on the newer CVSS 4.0 scale, though individual reports from companies like Oracle itself and Red Hat give it their own ratings , but they're all in the 8 to 9.8 range depending on the vendor. The root cause is a bug in OpenJDK, the library that nearly every distribution of Java, whether Oracle's or anyone else's, derives their implementations from. items.summary: Nvidia’s GeForce 621.14 and 621.24 drivers reportedly rewrite a log file nonstop, writing gigabytes to SSDs every hour.
items.body: Nvidia’s GeForce driver 621.14 is reportedly causing excessive background writes on idle PCs, inducing extra wear on SSDs. One user measured about 3GB an hour on the susceptible driver, and another mentioned estimated up to 30GB/hour on the newer 621.24. This follows a similar-looking bug from AMD’s video driver discovered last month. The bug is described by user Andergraude in an Nvidia forum post as “new in 621.14,” which came out on Nov. 4, who says it operates by “continuously [rewriting] the binary log file” with “real writes” to the drive. The writes are coming from the NVDisplay.Container.exe process, or the “NVIDIA Display Container LS” service, which logs to the nvlog.nvlgstg file. This background service is necessary for running the Nvidia Control Panel and App. It’s not clear what’s written in the log, and not every system is necessarily impacted. The “real writes” point comes from the fact that a per-process write counter is not the same as writes reaching the drive. items.body: While Ohioans have rejected the building of new data centers at every turn, they might not have much choice in the future. That's if a newly leaked bill that could allow data centers to be classified as public utilities is allowed to progress. The move would see the list of who can qualify for eminent domain law expanded, moving beyond entities owned or operated by municipal corporations, electric cooperatives, and agencies holding a certificate of public convenience and necessity granted by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. The bill, leaked to WCPO Cincinnati , would add "and an agency holding a certificate of environmental compatibility and public need from the power siting board for constructing an electric transmission line and associated facilities or gas pipeline and its associated facilities." Legal experts have warned that the change could mean a transmission developer, like a power company, would be able to seize land to be used for a data center or a facility that would power one. A countdown at Orbital Radar confirmed that Voyager cruised past the threshold at a leisurely 37,844 mph just after 5 am ET on Wednesday, November 18. There are many astronomical numbers behind what is an extraordinary feat. Sci-fi shows casually mention light-years as if they are like a trip to the local convenience store. One light-day isn’t a distance to be derided, though. The report observes a 20% drop in spot pricing for NAND chips over just the last month. Its conclusions are bolstered by information from a Bank of America note from Nov. 13, wherein industry sources tell that institution that NAND is due for a market correction. SED says that according to that note, 512 Gb NAND wafers saw a 32% drop to $14.30 apiece on the spot market, while 1 Tb wafers fell 19% to $24.90. SED quotes another industry source that says: "NAND cannot sustain the steep price gains seen so far." items.body: The City of Memphis has announced that it will make its first major investment as part of its new Community Benefits Ordinance. The fund will use revenue generated by taxing SpaceX AI's Colossus 1 facility to fund various initiatives within the South Memphis neighborhoods around that data center. The fund will help with the costs associated with housing, neighborhood improvements, and services, with the first $2 million allocated for the Memphis HOPE Initiative — a new home repair assistance program that helps residents make vital repairs as well as improvements that will make their homes more accessible. The HOPE Initiative will provide low- and moderate-income homeowners and even renters with up to $25,000 for qualifying repairs and improvements. Eligible improvements include structural repairs as well as plumbing, heating, and air conditioning repairs. Roof repairs and replacement, accessibility improvements, and some exterior improvements like painting, fencing, and landscaping are also eligible. items.summary: Nvidia's Vera CPU, powered by its custom Olympus Arm cores, already offers strong performance with unoptimized code, but at SC26, the company demonstrated that further software optimizations can improve performance by nearly 39% with certain workloads.
items.body: Nvidia's Vera CPU, designed as both a standalone data-center part and a host for Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 servers, offers impressive performance thanks to substantially higher execution resources per core than its predecessor, Grace. However, Nvidia admits at Supercomputing 2026 (SC26) that existing software cannot always take full advantage of Vera's resources without adaptation for the architecture. The company shared that architecture-specific software optimizations can boost Vera's performance by nearly 39% in certain computationally intensive workloads. But despite offering unbeatable single-thread performance, the CPU is not positioned for general-purpose workloads. items.title: AMD attacks Nvidia's FP64 emulation at SC26, touts native double-precision on Instinct MI430X
items.summary: AMD is touting the benefits of the native FP64 support provided by its MI430X accelerator at Supercomputing 2026. The company says that Ozaki FP64 emulation only covers the needs of a small portion of HPC workloads, making the MI430X a unique foundation for next-gen supercomputing installations.
items.body: As Supercomputing 2026 (SC26) opens in Chicago this week, AMD is indirectly needling Nvidia about the lack of native FP64 data type support in its data center GPU products. FP64, or double-precision floating-point math, is widely used in the high-performance scientific computing and simulation fields that are the focus of SC26. For those customers, AMD is trumpeting the value of its latest Instinct MI430X accelerator for customers that still need native FP64, like national laboratories and supercomputing centers. Over the past few years, Nvidia has reallocated die area on its data center GPUs to favor the lower-precision matrix math that boosts the operations needed for much of modern AI inference. That reallocation only makes business sense, as the total addressable market for AI compute has exploded while the demand for double-precision math in large supercomputing installations has remained flat by comparison. To make up for the lack of native FP64 support, Nvidia has turned to techniques that allow it to emulate FP64 operations using methods like the Ozaki schemes. items.title: Phison Pascari X201P 15.36TB SSD Review: Fast PCIe 5.0 write performance for AI and ingest servers
items.summary: The Phison Pascari X201P 15.36TB U.2 data center SSD meets its rated speeds and saves AI checkpoints quickly, though it trails on low-queue-depth writes.
items.body: Phison is serious about enterprise storage, and the Pascari X201P was not released lightly; it came in the night, under NDA, alongside this week’s Supercomputing 2026 event. The drive is part of the Performance X-Series, which handles intensive workloads where consistency is the name of the game. We were nevertheless pleasantly surprised by its write performance, with a steady 12 GB/s for sequential and over 600,000 random write IOPS, considering it’s marketed at the 1 drive write per day (DWPD) endurance point. Part of that surprise comes from the fact that this is Phison’s read-intensive PCIe 5.0 data center drive, a successor to the X200P. It comes in the U.2 form factor — which can be more convenient in many cases — from 1.92TB to 30.72TB, and an E3.S version from 3.84TB, in both single- and dual-port models. It stands next to its mixed-use sibling, the X201E, which is the one rated for 3 DWPD. What makes the X201P exciting, in part, is its own 16-channel X2 controller and the flash that’s inside.
